newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Mass unrest looms as Colombia unions vote strike.
newsitem.headline: Mass unrest looms as Colombia unions vote strike.

text.p: Colombia's main unions agreed Friday to launch a nationwide strike, raising the specter of severe social unrest just four days after the government declared a state of economic emergency.

The bad news for the embattled government of President Ernesto Samper was coupled with a decision by the country's leading business group, the National Business Council, to boycott a new wage and price control pact to protest new tax laws.

Labor leaders from all key economic and social sectors -- communications, oil, health, education, justice and public administration -- passed the strike motion after a day-long meeting in Bogota. The starting date for the action, set to be the biggest since 1977, will be fixed for either Feb. 4 or Feb. 11 at a meeting Monday, union bosses said.

Samper declared a 20-day state of economic emergency Monday and introduced a series of belt-tightening measures to slash public spending and increase tax revenues in a bid to rein in Colombia's growing fiscal deficit.

The unions, which together represent about 35 percent of the Colombian labor force, are pressing for fresh negotiations on public and private sector salary raises, which the government set unilaterally after leaders pulled out of social pact talks at the end of December.
